chapter.title: Estimation, Hypothesis Tests and Confidence Procedures

sections.title: Likelihood estimation, sufficiency, consistency and efficiency

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: Fisher p. 322's standard error pi/(2 sqrt n) for the median of a large Cauchy sample is not stated with explicit model, sampling and regularity scope or proved. It needs asymptotic normality of the sample median with variance pi^2/(4n). fisher-estimation-and-regularity.tex 304-321 proves only consistency.

ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: Fisher p. 317's fourfold-table example (a double dichotomy of a normal surface, where the criterion of consistency determines the correlation uniquely) is not reconstructed with model, sampling and uniqueness scope or a proof.

ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: Fisher's location and scale efficiency contours on the Type I/II side of the normal point (figs. 3-4, pp. 346-347) are not shown to be the efficiencies of those curves. Owned body 1130-1133 says they rest on Fisher's calculation alone.

ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: Fisher p. 355 says moments are at least 80 per cent efficient for the form exactly when beta_2 lies in [2.65, 3.42]. This needs E_r to be monotone in r on each side, which is not proved (owned body 1438-1442).

ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: For the Type II form parameters (pp. 354-355), condition (C) is not verified. So the inverse-information values are not shown to be the limit variances of a root of the likelihood equations (owned body 1443-1447).

ED26-METHOD-likelihood-estimation-C03: Fisher p. 337 says Type III location at p=1 is determined faster than sqrt n whether or not p and a are known. The case with unknown scale and unknown shape is not proved (owned body 1607-1611; thm:p15-w02b-p15-057-linear-end assumes a and the shape are known).
